claim: At N=256, e<=0.5 (seeds 65-69), accel_step crosses the 0.1 margin and stays above it at steps 100/100/100/100/125 (seeds 65/66/68/69/67, read from the trajectories), and reaches half of its final margin at steps 75/95/85/95/120. The N=64 arm for the same seeds formed at 65-90 (0.1 bar) and 40-70 (half-final), so every N=256 seed is at least +10 steps later on the 0.1 bar, with a mean delay of roughly +15 to +40; the per-seed >=+15 test could not be checked because the paired per-seed N=64 values were not available. Final accel_step R2 is 0.853-0.900 vs controls 0.685-0.726 (margins 0.162-0.175), while force ends with no margin (-0.004 to 0.051, beats_control false in all 5) after an early transient of 0.17-0.23 at steps 10-20, and no run beats the baseline (val_mse_ratio 11.8-14.2).
confidence_note: The direction is consistent: the earliest N=256 formation step (100) is later than the latest N=64 step for these seeds (90). The refutation pattern did not happen, because the 0.1-bar delay is >=+10 in all 5 seeds and the half-final delay can be <=+10 only for seed 65 (N=256 half-final step 75; it first crosses at 75, dips at 80, and stays above from 85). But the experiment is defined on per-seed pairs, and this analysis only had the N=64 range (65-90 / 40-70) from open-question summaries, not the per-seed values in f-20261012-054929-0067. That file was not readable here, the same failure as q-20261012-052949-98cc. Using those ranges as bounds, the pooled 11-seed mean delay is about +19.5 to +31 on the 0.1 bar (earlier deltas +20/+70/+30/0/0/+20) and about +23 or more on half-final. Both bounds straddle or barely clear the +20 criterion. Seed 68's probes_final.formed_at_step is 105, but its trajectory crosses at 100, the same one-checkpoint lag as q-20261012-032843-df65; trajectory values are used here. Joining the per-seed N=64 trajectories would most likely turn this into supported. It would stay inconclusive or flip if two or more N=64 seeds formed at 90 on the 0.1 bar. Formation at N=256 again happens while the model is about 12x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation, so it says nothing about task success.
